reviewStatus: DRAFT — this letter list is a placeholder drawn from published descriptions of the Montana Salish sound system. It is waiting to be replaced by the Séliš-Ql̓ispé alphabet as taught in the ILFTS curriculum. Not for classroom use until that swap is made.

categories.name: Stops & Affricates
categories.description: The air is stopped completely somewhere in the mouth, then released.

categories.name: Fricatives
categories.description: The air is squeezed through a narrow gap and hisses or rushes.

categories.name: Resonants
categories.description: The voice keeps running through the sound. Each one has a glottalized partner.

categories.name: Vowels
categories.description: The mouth is open and the voice shapes the sound.

letters.howTo: Bring both lips together so the air stops completely, then open them and let the air out. Like the p in "spin" — no puff of breath after it.
letters.watchFor: Watch the lips press flat together, then part cleanly.

letters.howTo: Close both lips and close your throat at the same time. Push the trapped air up with your voice box, then pop the lips open. It comes out as a sharp little pop, not a puff.
letters.watchFor: Watch the throat tighten before the lips release — the pop is louder and shorter than plain p.

letters.howTo: Press the tip of the tongue against the ridge just behind the upper teeth, stop the air, then release it.
letters.watchFor: Watch the tongue tip come forward to the teeth ridge.

letters.howTo: Set the tongue tip behind the upper teeth and close your throat at the same time. Squeeze the trapped air, then release the tongue for a sharp popping t.
letters.watchFor: The jaw stays still while the throat does the work.

letters.howTo: Say the ts at the end of "cats". The tongue tip stops the air behind the teeth, then releases into a hiss.
letters.watchFor: Teeth stay close together through the whole sound.

letters.howTo: Make the ts sound, but close your throat first and squeeze the air upward, so it snaps out sharply.
letters.watchFor: Listen for the snap — the hiss is much shorter than plain c.

letters.howTo: Say the ch in "church". The tongue blade stops the air just behind the teeth ridge, then releases into a sh sound.
letters.watchFor: The lips push forward slightly.

letters.howTo: Make the ch sound with the throat closed, squeezing the trapped air so it bursts out sharply.
letters.watchFor: Watch the throat move up just before the release.

letters.howTo: Raise the back of the tongue to the soft palate and round the lips at the same time, like the qu in "quick".
letters.watchFor: The lips round before the sound is released — the rounding is part of the letter.

letters.howTo: Set up the rounded kʷ, close the throat, squeeze the air, then release it sharply.
letters.watchFor: Rounded lips plus a sharp popping release.

letters.howTo: Like k, but much farther back. The very back of the tongue presses against the uvula, deep in the throat.
letters.watchFor: The jaw drops a little and the sound is deeper and duller than k.

letters.howTo: Make the deep q closure, close the throat below it, squeeze, and release with a sharp pop.
letters.watchFor: The whole throat lifts before the release.

letters.howTo: Make the deep q sound while rounding the lips at the same time.
letters.watchFor: Lips round while the sound stays deep in the throat.

letters.howTo: Rounded lips, deep q closure, closed throat — squeeze the air and pop it out.
letters.watchFor: Rounding plus the sharp deep pop.

letters.howTo: Close your throat and cut the sound off completely. It is the catch in the middle of "uh-oh".
letters.watchFor: Nothing moves in the mouth — all the work is in the throat.

letters.howTo: Tongue tip near the ridge behind the upper teeth, teeth close together, and let the air hiss through.
letters.watchFor: Teeth nearly touching, lips spread.

letters.howTo: Put your tongue where you would for l — tip on the ridge behind the teeth — but instead of using your voice, blow air out over the sides of the tongue.
letters.watchFor: The tongue tip stays up the whole time; the air escapes around the sides, not the middle.

letters.howTo: Say the sh in "ship". The tongue blade is a little farther back than for s and the lips push forward.
letters.watchFor: Lips rounded and pushed forward.

letters.howTo: Raise the back of the tongue toward the soft palate, round the lips, and blow — like blowing out a candle with a whispered wh.
letters.watchFor: Steady rounded lips with a continuous rush of air.

letters.howTo: Pull the back of the tongue toward the uvula and let the air rasp past it. It sounds like gently clearing the throat.
letters.watchFor: The mouth is fairly open — the sound is made deep in the throat, not at the lips.

letters.howTo: Make the deep rasping x̌ sound while rounding the lips at the same time.
letters.watchFor: Rounded lips with the rasp still coming from the throat.

letters.howTo: Open the mouth and breathe out, letting the air brush past the open throat.
letters.watchFor: The mouth is already in position for the next vowel.

letters.howTo: Close both lips and hum — the voice comes out through the nose.
letters.watchFor: Lips stay shut and the sound keeps going.

letters.howTo: Hum the m, but squeeze your throat closed in the middle of it so the hum is pinched or interrupted.
letters.watchFor: The lips do not move — the catch happens in the throat.

letters.howTo: Tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth, voice running out through the nose.
letters.watchFor: Mouth slightly open, tongue tip up.

letters.howTo: Make the n sound and squeeze the throat closed during it, so the voice catches.
letters.watchFor: Tongue holds still while the throat pinches the sound.

letters.howTo: Tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth, voice flowing out around the sides of the tongue.
letters.watchFor: Tongue tip visible against the teeth ridge.

letters.howTo: Make the l sound with a catch in the throat partway through.
letters.watchFor: The tongue never leaves the ridge.

letters.howTo: Voiced r made with the tongue tip toward the ridge behind the teeth. It is not the English r — ask your teacher to show the tongue position.
letters.watchFor: Watch the tongue tip closely; this one is easy to substitute an English sound for.

letters.howTo: Make the r sound with a catch in the throat partway through.
letters.watchFor: Tongue position holds while the throat pinches.

letters.howTo: Round the lips tightly and raise the back of the tongue, then glide into the next sound, as in "water".
letters.watchFor: Tight lip rounding at the start.

letters.howTo: Make the rounded w with a catch in the throat during it.
letters.watchFor: Lips hold their round shape through the catch.

letters.howTo: Raise the front of the tongue toward the roof of the mouth and glide, as in "yes".
letters.watchFor: Lips spread wide, tongue high in front.

letters.howTo: Make the y glide with a catch in the throat during it.
letters.watchFor: Spread lips held through the catch.

letters.howTo: Tighten the very back of the throat — the pharynx — and keep your voice going through it. It has a squeezed, growly quality.
letters.watchFor: Little happens at the lips; watch the throat and the jaw dropping.

letters.howTo: Make the squeezed throat sound with a catch in the middle of it.
letters.watchFor: The throat tightens twice — once for the sound, once for the catch.

letters.howTo: Make the squeezed throat sound while rounding the lips at the same time.
letters.watchFor: Rounded lips with the growly throat sound behind them.

letters.howTo: Rounded lips, squeezed throat, and a catch in the middle of the sound.
letters.watchFor: Rounding held through the catch.

letters.howTo: Open the mouth wide and drop the tongue low, like the a in "father".
letters.watchFor: The jaw drops farthest for this vowel.

letters.howTo: Front of the tongue mid-high, lips spread, like the e in "bet" held steady.
letters.watchFor: Lips spread, jaw only part way open.

letters.howTo: Front of the tongue high and lips spread wide, like the ee in "see".
letters.watchFor: Widest lip spread, smallest jaw opening.

letters.howTo: Back of the tongue mid-high with rounded lips, like the o in "go" held steady without gliding.
letters.watchFor: Round lips that do not change shape partway through.

letters.howTo: Back of the tongue high with tightly rounded lips, like the oo in "boot".
letters.watchFor: Tightest lip rounding of all the vowels.

letters.howTo: A short, relaxed vowel made with the tongue resting in the middle of the mouth — the uh in "sofa".
letters.watchFor: The mouth barely moves; this vowel is quick and unstressed.
